result.title: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360° via Outpainting
result.comment: Accepted at BMVC 2026. 22 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: https://finlay-hudson.github.io/tapout/
result.summary: Tracking points that leave the camera's field of view (FoV) requires reasoning about unobserved scene dynamics, a fundamentally different problem from tracking visible correspondences. We present TAP-Out, an offline method that makes this out-of-view (OOV) reasoning explicit by leveraging generative video outpainting as a world-model prior. Given a narrow-FoV input video, TAP-Out outpaints a complete 360° equirectangular video, locates target objects within the panoramic scene via video object segmentation, and synthesises object-centred perspective crops on which standard in-frame trackers operate. This decoupled design composes off-the-shelf foundation models without requiring task-specific architectural modifications. On the TAPVid360 benchmark, TAP-Out achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving OOV tracking accuracy by approximately 3x over the best prior method. We demonstrate its flexibility on out-of-frame object segmentation and detection and we provide detailed diagnostic analyses across motion regimes, static versus dynamic content, and hallucination quality, characterising when and why the approach succeeds or fails.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TAP-Out 离线流程：先用视频外扩把窄视野输入补成 360° 全景，再经视频目标分割定位目标并合成以目标为中心的透视裁剪，交给现成帧内跟踪器，从而处理目标离开视野后的点跟踪，并在 TAPVid360 上报告约 3 倍于此前方法的视野外精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把「视野外场景动态」从隐式推理改为显式生成像素证据，并诊断生成内容质量，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据获取与筛选、以及显式视觉旁路是否优于内部 latent 表示的问题形成对照，可供核查；但任务是点跟踪，不涉及推理期 latent 状态或答案对 latent 的使用。
